# The grouped block for the first invoice, on a wire that also settles another
# and leaves a residue.
#
# It names the −60.00 and −40.00 that settle this invoice and declares the
# 50.00 left over. The −180.00 beside them is the other invoice's portion,
# already in that record's lot.
#
# This is the block the export writes for this state, and it was refused by the
# importer that received it: the residue check totalled every receivable split
# the block did not name — the other invoice's 180.00 among them — and made
# 230.00 of a 50.00 residue. The writer skips a split sitting in a lot that
# names an invoice or a bill, because that is that record's portion and was
# never left over, and the reader has to ask the same question.
#
# What this fixture produces: both splits applied in this invoice's lot, the
# 50.00 parked as the customer's credit, and the other invoice untouched.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-03-24
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    prepayment: 50
    Transaction "77aa11bb22cc33dd44ee55ff66007788"
      PaymentSplit "99aa11bb22cc33dd44ee55ff66007722"
      PaymentSplit "aaaa11bb22cc33dd44ee55ff66007733"
